summary: US-005: QR e-ticket issued and delivered
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** my ticket with a QR code by email and on a web page after purchase. Mailer is a port with log transport (brief non-goal: no notifications service).

**Priority:** P1
**Depends on:** US-004 (TKT-28)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Access service issues a signed QR payload per paid ticket, triggered by the order-completed event
- [ ] Mailer port (log transport) records a delivery with ticket link; buyer ticket page renders the QR (browser-verified)
- [ ] Issuance and delivery are recorded as append-only ticket lifecycle events linked to the order (ADR-003); the ticket's history is queryable; lifecycle events carry pseudonymous IDs only — delivery address resolved from the PII store at send time
- [ ] Tickets are re-retrievable by order reference (guest flow, no account)

Quality gates: `make check` green (defined in US-001, mirrors CI); contract tests for touched service boundaries; UI: browser-verified with screenshot in PR; money paths: NF525 journal chain verifies (from US-004).

binding.rule: We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

Append-only trails, one discipline: (1) money journal — every money-relevant record immutable, sequence-numbered, hash-chained, signed; corrections are compensating entries; read models are projections; verify-journal in the local gate from US-004. (2) ticket lifecycle trace — every ticket/entitlement state change is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order; redemption/reissue decisions are made from the trace. (3) trails are pseudonymous: records reference customers by pseudonymous ID only, PII lives in a separate erasable store; no raw PII in any append-only record (enforced invariant from US-004). (4) NF525 is a later-phase profile that must layer on without schema or flow changes.

comments.body: Scope amended pre-Gate-1 (owner directive 2026-07-12): NF525 is NOT an immediate goal — it becomes a later-phase French-market profile. The underlying requirement is generalized: traceability is a must, with the same audit-trail thinking for money AND tickets (ADR-003 reworked accordingly). New AC: issuance/delivery recorded as append-only lifecycle events.
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): lifecycle events pseudonymous per amended ADR-003.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed after owner acceptance of TKT-28 (2026-07-13). TKT-29 is the next unblocked walking-skeleton story and P1 dependency for TKT-30. It will establish the access-service issuance/delivery boundary, with pseudonymous lifecycle events per ADR-003; plan review applies.

objective.note: US-005 acceptance criteria specify signed QR issuance, log delivery, pseudonymous lifecycle trace, and guest re-retrieval.

scope.note: In: access issuance, delivery port/log transport, ticket/history and guest retrieval surfaces, Commerce event/PII seam, storefront ticket page, contracts/tests/evidence. Out: accounts wallet, rotating barcodes/PDF/real email (TKT-18), scanner behavior (TKT-30).

uncertainties.note: Delivery-event reliability, QR signing/key lifecycle, and safe PII lookup are design decisions to resolve and record during planning; no external dependency blocks them.

dependencies.note: TKT-28 is Done; PR #7 established the order-completed event, pseudonymous buyer correlation, separate Commerce PII store, and verified journal.

approach.note: Contract-first and event-driven: consume completed orders idempotently, issue opaque signed ticket QR payloads, append immutable lifecycle events, resolve PII only at mail-send boundary.

first_slice.note: One coherent vertical slice: completed checkout produces a retrievable QR ticket and log-mail delivery, verified through gateway/browser and lifecycle history.

success.note: All US-005 ACs, contracts, browser screenshot, populated journal verification, and make check green.
